gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, priced at the makers' US stores on 2026-11-15, two of ChatGPT's own long-runtime picks cannot ship now: the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus ($3,499) is on pre-order until Nov 28, and the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus page shows Sold Out. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra ($3,799) is listed as unavailable. Among systems you can order, the BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K (5,529.6 Wh, $2,599) costs about $83 per hour of 150 W pellet-stove runtime. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X (12,288 Wh, $7,899) costs about $113 per hour, but it is the longest-running unit in stock.
standout_why: Solarwaypoint (cited) lists capacity and maximum expansion for the F3800, Apex 300 and DELTA Pro, but its comparison has no prices and no stock status. ChatGPT's answers show capacity and runtime with one example price ($4,199). They give no stock status and no cost per hour of runtime. I could not open the two cited EnoughWatts pages (TLS certificate error), so I can't rule out that they show prices. Our current page prices only the DELTA 2 Max.
decides: The longest-running system you can buy today is the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X standard bundle: 12,288 Wh, about 70 h at 150 W, $7,899, in stock. ChatGPT's first chat carded the DELTA Pro Ultra, which is listed as unavailable. In the second chat, the next two by runtime (Jackery 5000 Plus, Anker F3800 Plus) are on pre-order or sold out. For a shopper who wants multi-day runtime without paying for a whole-home system, the in-stock BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K gives about 31 h for $2,599. That is less than half the price of the DELTA Pro Ultra X, with a lower cost per hour. The BLUETTI Elite 300 ($1,199, about 17 h) is the cheapest per hour of runtime but covers only one night.

findings.label: Maker price and stock, standard bundle (1 inverter + 2 Smart Extra Batteries, 12 kWh)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Whole-Home Backup Power
findings.note: Read through the store's Shopify product data (storecheck search). The page states '12kW/12kWh based on standard bundle (1 × EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X Inverter + 2 × Smart Extra Batteries)', and each battery is 6,144 Wh (battery listing), so 12,288 Wh. Runtime: 12,288 × 0.85 / 150 W = 69.6 h, which works out to $113 per hour of runtime. Where it loses: it costs about 3× the Apex 300 + B300K for about 2.2× the runtime, and it is sold as a whole-home system that EcoFlow says is 'installed in 7 days'.

findings.label: Maker price and stock (inverter + 1 battery, 6,144 Wh)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra Whole-Home Backup Power (UL 9540 Certificated)
findings.note: The store's Shopify data returned available=false for this product. The 1 inverter + 2 batteries listing ($5,999) and the Starter Kit ($2,099) also returned available=false. Runtime: 6,144 × 0.85 / 150 = 34.8 h, which works out to $109/h. Where it loses: you can't order it from the maker today, even though ChatGPT carded it as the longest-running pick.

findings.label: Maker price and stock
findings.note: The listing text says 'Sold out due to high demand. Pre-order now, ships Nov 28.' and gives the capacity as 5,040 Wh. The '10kWh' and 'Double Kit (10kWh)' listings also returned a $3,499 lead price, which is probably the lowest variant price, so treat $3,499 as the single-unit figure. The variant-level product lookup was rate-limited. Runtime: 5,040 × 0.85 / 150 = 28.6 h, which works out to $122/h. Where it loses: it won't ship until Nov 28, and it costs the most per hour of runtime of the units I priced.
